headline: Oilers' Brett Epp dresses as full-time emergency backup goalie
take:
ESPN reports that the Oilers became the first NHL team to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie on Thursday night against Anaheim, with Brett Epp in that role. The headline and summary don't say more than that, so we won't guess at the reason.

The more useful question is what the goaltending behind the story looks like. EDM sit at 11-2-3 with 25 points in 16 games, and their share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality for versus against) is 52 percent so far this season. They've scored 18.1 goals more than expected, but their goalies are 2.4 goals below expected in saves. So the results lean on finishing, not on the crease. At five-on-five, expected goal share drops to 49 percent, which means the edge comes from special teams. The power play generates 0.88 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.52. If goaltending stays shaky, depth in net matters more than usual.
